Criteria for sanction of Grant-in-aid 
A. Strengthening of the existing undergraduate colleges of I.S.M. & H.: 
(1) The Institutions/Colleges should have been duly permitted by 
CCIM/CCH; 
(2) The Institutions/Colleges should have completed 5 years of 
existence and at least one batch of students should have 
successfully come out of the Institutions; 
(3) The Institution/College should have a minimum admission of 30 
students at least every year; 
(4) There should be regular turnover of graduated students; 
(5) There should be a functioning teaching hospital with at least 60% 
bed occupancy; 
(6) Priority should be given to Government/Government-aided 
Institutions/Colleges; 
(7) There should be at least 50% of the prescribed teaching staff in 
position; 
(8) The Government-aided college/private college must be registered 
under the Societies Registration Act or PublicTrust Act; 
(9) Relaxation may be considered for Colleges/Institutions in the 
North-Eastern States/Sikkim and J&K; and 
(10)   No Objection Certificate from the concerned State Governments. 
B. SCHEME FOR UPGRADATION OF POSTGRADUATE 
DEPARTMENT OF I.S.M. & H: 
(1) The college should be affiliated to a recognized university in the 
State; 
(2) Only those Departments shall be considered for upgradation which 
have the necessary infrastructure for undergraduate level as required 
by CCIM; 
4 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
(3) The curriculum and syllabus for the postgraduate course in the 
subject be in accordance with the curriculum and syllabus 
prescribed by the CCIM; 
(4) The department should be off all-India character and 50% seats should 
be kept reserved for students from outside, if forthcoming. 
Necessary reservation shall be made for SC/ST candidates as per 
Government policy; 
(5) Filling of the all teaching posts will be by regular modes of 
recruitment, namely, competitive selection by advertisements of all-
India nature; and' 
(6) Yearly admissions for postgraduate training in one department shall 
be limited 6 to 7 students every year in a manner to be decided by 
the college authorities, so that at a time there are not more than 20 
postgraduate students in all the three years. 
Educational low-powered FM radio stations 
*402. SHRIEDUARDO FALEIRO: Will the Minister of INFORMATION 
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have received proposals from universities or 
deemed universities to run educational low-powered FM radio stations; 
(b) if so, the decision taken on the same; 
(c) the progress in setting up 40 ratio stations of the IGNOU in various 
parts of the country; 
(d) the cities/States where these stations have been set up, and the places 
where these are yet to be set up; and 
(e) the funds made available for this purpose? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 
(SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) For the present, the Government have allowed Indira Gandhi 
National Open University (IGNOU), under the Ministry of Human Resource 
Development to run FM radio stations for educational programmes. 
5 

RAJYA  SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
(c) and (d) Ministry of Human Resource Development has informed that 6 
radio stations have been commissioned at Allahabad, Bangalore, 
Visakhpatnam, Coimbatore, Lucknow and Mumbai. The 7th station at 
Bhopal is likely to be commissioned shortly. 23 stations are likely to be 
commissioned during 2002-03. The remaining 10 stations will be 
commissioned during the next financial year. 
(e) A provision of Rs. 15.10 crores was made during the year 2001-02.  
Incidence of kidney stones 
*403. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news-item 
captioned, "North India's eating habits, climate cause kidney stones" which 
appeared in the 'HindustanTimes' dated 26th July, 2002; 
(b) whether it is a fact that the incidence of kidney stones is rising in Delhi 
and adjoining States mainly because people here consume fatty, milk-based 
food and a lot of fried food whereas South Indians eat steamed food; 
(c) if so, whether Government propose to use electronic media to make 
the public aware of all such diseases; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b)The dietary habits and climatic conditions influence formation of 
kidney stone. The incidence of kidney stone is relatively high in Delhi and 
adjoining State. There are, however, no specific studies to show any rising 
trend in the incidence of kidney stones in Delhi and adjoining areas. 
(c) and (d) Creating public awareness through media about various 
diseases, is continuous process. However, the patients visiting various Central 
Government Hospitals/AIIMS are given counselling on proper nutrition and 
the food habits. 
6 

 [12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
Punishment for construction of dry latrines 
*404. SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of 
URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether construction of dry latrines is unlawful under the 
Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines 
(Prohibition) Act, 1993; 
(b) if so, the number of people punished/fined for construction of dry 
latrines since the enactment of the Act, State-wise; 
(c) the reasons for implementation of this Act only in fifteen States at 
present; and 
(d) the steps taken to impress upon all the States to adopt and properly 
implement this Act? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI ANANTH KUMAR): (a)Yes, Sir. 
(b) No such data is compiled in this Ministry. 
(c)The subject Sanitation falls under Entry 6 of List II (State List) of 
the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. The Employment of 
Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993 
was enacted by the Parliament under Article 252 when State Legislatures of 
Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tripura and Goa 
passed Resolutions empowering the Parliament to enact a Legislation for 
abolishing manual scavenging by declaring employment of manual 
scavengers for removal of human excreta an offence and thereby prevent 
further proliferation of dry latrines. The said Act, which has been passed by 
the Parliament under Article 252 (i), will be applicable only to those States 
which adopt this Act. At present, Act is applicable to 17 States and in all the 
UnionTerritories. 
(d) the State Governments have been urged from time to time to take 
steps towards adoption/implementation of this Act through communications 
addressed to the State Governments at various levels and also by highlighting 
this during meetings held in this Ministry from time to time. 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
Extension of purchase preference policy 
*405. SHRI K.M. KHAN: Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have decided to extend the purchase 
preference policy for products and sevices of Central PSUs, which had expired 
on 31 st March, 2002; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the steps taken by Government to make PSUs efficient, 
competitive and self-supporting? 
THE MINISTER OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC 
ENTERPRISES (SHRI BALASAHEBVIKHE PATIL): (a) to (c) Government 
have decided to extend the existing purchase preference policy for products 
and services of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) for two more years 
from 1.4.2002 to 31.3.2004 and issued guidelines on 14.6.2002. Under the 
policy, if the price quoted by the public sector enterprise is within 10% of the 
lowest price in a tender, other things being equal, purchase preference may be 
granted to the CPSE concerned at the lowest valid price bid. The policy has the 
following provisions: 
(i) the 10% purchase preference would bo extended to tenders/ NIT of 
rupees five crores and above. 
(ii) CPSEs registered under the Companies Act, 1956 and statutory CPSEs 
will be eligible for purchase preference as before. Joint venture 
companies where holding of Government and/or CPSEs is 51% or 
more and joint ventures which are subsidiaries of CPSEs with 
CPSEs holding 51% equity or more will also be eligible for 
purchase preference. 
(iii) A minimum value addition of 20% by the CPSEs/joint venture units 
by way of manufacture and/or services would be a prerequisite for 
availing purchase preference. 
(iv) Ministries/Departments/CPSEs and autonomous bodies under Central 
Government will continue to grant purchase preference to CPSEs. 
8 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
(v) Purchase preference will also be available to only those privatized 
CPSEs where specific Government approval has been accorded 
for the specific periods from the date of disinvestment. 
(vi) Respective Ministries/Departments/autonomous bodies/ CPSEs 
will be responsible for implementing the Purchase Preference 
Policy. 
(vii) As per the existing policy the provisions relating to purchase 
preference should be specified in the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) 
for rupees five crores and above. For any deviation including 
exclusion of the purchase preference clause from the NIT, it will 
be obligatory for the concerned Ministry/ 
Department/CPSES/autonomous bodies to obtain prior exemption 
from the Cabinet in consultation with the Department of Public 
Enterprises. 
(viii) Other provisions of the purchase preference policy remain unaltered. 
(d) Various steps are taken to make the Central Public Sector 
Enterprises (CPSEs) more efficient, competitive and self-supporting in the 
liberalised economic environment. Some of the steps include delegation of 
enhanced powers and greater operational autonomy through the mechanism of 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Navratna/Mini-ratna schemes, 
professionalisation of Board of Directors, reduction of centralised guidelines, 
business and financial restructuring, formation of joint ventures, modernisation of 
plant and machinery, upgradation of technology, purchase preference, 
rationalisation of manpower through Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) etc.

Labelling on Soft Drinks 
407. SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN: Will the Minister of HEALTH 
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the harmful effects of 
carbonated soft drinks on health and their habit-forming nature; 
(b) whether Government are also aware that many foreign countries make it 
mandatory to label soft drink bottles and cans with warning about presence of 
caffeine, calorie content and the type and amount of sweetener used; 
(c) whether Government have conducted any study to find out which 
foreign country has regulations for such compulsory markings; 
(d) whether Government have any plan of introducing such mandatory 
labelling of soft drinks in the country; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) Carbonated beverages conforming to the 
standards as laid down under PFA Rules, 1955, are safe for human consumption. 
(b) to (e) Government is  aware of the lebelling regulations prevalent in 
foreign countries. Specific labelling provisions have been prescribed under 
PFA Rules, 1955, at par with International Labelling Provisions for 
12 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA    SABHA 
those products containing artificial sweeteners. Following additional labelling 
requirements for these products are under process:- 
(i) A declaration "Contains caffeine." 
(ii) A declaration "quantity of sugar added." 
(iii) A declaration "no sugar added" in the product. 
(iv) Product containing artificial sweeteners shall be packed and sold 
with all the prescribed declarations on the body of the containers. 
These products shall not be packed and sold in returnable glass 
containers where prescribed label declarations cannot be incorporated 
on the body of the containers. 
Cheaper Hepatitis-B vaccine 
408.      SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: 
SHRI RAJU PARMAR: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Hepatitis-B spreads very easily and one in 
every twenty Indians is already infected with this killer disease; 
(b) if so, the steps Government have taken or propose to take for 
protection against this disease; 
(c) whether cheap vaccines are available in the country for the poor; and 
(d) if not, the steps being taken to procure Hepatitis-B vaccines at 
cheaper rates? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (d) Hepatitis-B spreads through 
unsafe sex, unsafe blood transfusion, unsafe injections etc. and also from 
mother to child. Hepatitis-B is preventable by ensuring precautionary measures. 
Studies undertaken so far, indicate that about 3% to 5% of the population in the 
country is suffering from Hepatitis-B infection.The following 
13 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
measures have been taken to prevent infection of Hepatitis-B:- 
• Central Government hospitals personnel at high risk are being 
immunized against Hepatitis-B. State Governments have also been 
advised to take similar steps. 
• Guidelines have been issued for mandatory testing of blood in all 
blood banks. 
• Promotion of safe sex under National AIDS Control Programme is 
advocated. 
• Health awareness campaigns regarding the danger of using 
unsterile syringes and needles under National AIDS Control 
Programme are held. 
• Guidlines have been issued to State Health Authorities for use of 
separate sterile syringes and needles for each injection. 
• A pilot project to introduce Hepatitis-B Vaccine in 15 selected cities 
and 32 districts in 17 States of the country, which are high risk areas, 
in order to study the impact of administration has been launched. 
The pilot project is estimated to cost Rs. 27.19 crores out of which 
vaccines and AD syringes cost Rs. 23.89 crores, which will be 
funded by the Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization 
(GAVI). 
Vaccines for Hepatitis-B is available in the country at affordable prices.

'Doctor' in their names in India;

14

Control on DDA 
*412. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the State Government of Delhi has sought the 
control of Delhi Development Authority; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the reaction of Government thereto; 
(c) whether there is any other development authority in the States which 
is functioning under Government; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI ANANTH KUMAR): (a) to (d)The Delhi Legislative 
Assembly in its sitting held on 18.7.2002 has passed the following Resolution: 
"This House recommends that the Delhi Development Authority be transferred to 
Delhi Government with immediate effect." 
16 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
Delhi is not a State. It is a UnionTerritory with an elected Legislative 
Assembly. The powers given to the Legislative Assembly of the National 
Capital Territory of Delhi are in consonance with the provisions of 
Constitution (69th Amendment) Act, 1991. In terms of Article 246 (4) of the 
Constitution, Parliament is competent and has over-riding powers to enact any 
law for the Union Territories on any subject mentioned in the 7th Schedule to the 
Constitution of India. Moreover, by virtue of specific provision under Article 
239-AA 3a entries 1,2 and 18 of the State List and entry 64,65 and 66 of 
Concurrent List, insofar as they relate to entries 1, 2 and 18 have been reserved 
for Government of India. Entry 18 deals with subject of land. The Government of 
NCT of Delhi is not competent to legislate on matters relating to land, which is 
in the domain of Government of India. 
The Delhi Development Authority is a creature of the statute called Delhi 
Development Act, 1957 and as long as the constitutional provision exists and the 
subject matter is in the domain of the Union Government, the administration of 
this Act, and the control of DDA will continue with the Government of India. 
Keeping the above facts in view, the Resolution passed by the Delhi 
Assembly cannot be accepted by the Central Government The above said 
constitutional provisions relating to land matters are specific for NCT of Delhi. 
Since the other State Governments are competent to legislate on matters 
relating to land under their domain, development authorities in other States 
function under the respective State Governments. 
Arbitrary Power of Estate Officers 
*413. SHRI C.RTHIRUNAVUKKARASU: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have issued new norms to limit the arbitrary use of 
powers by the Estate Officers for eviction from public premises; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the reasons for formulating new norms? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI ANANTH KUMAR): (a) No, Sir. 
17 

RAJYA   SABh'A [12 August, 2002] 
(b) and (c) Following receipt of several representations forwarded by 
Hon'ble Ministers/Members of Parliament as well a? Tenants Associations, alleging 
misuse of the provisions of the Public Pi^mises (Eviction of Unauthorized 
Occupants) Act, 1971 by some Public Sector Undertakings and Government 
Financial Organisations in evicting theirbona-fide tenants, it was decided to set up 
an inter-Ministerial Committee, headed by the Director of Estates, to look into 
the complaints and make recommendations to avoid any misuse of the P.P. (E) Act, 
1971 .The Committee after holding detailed discussions with all affected parties 
including representatives of the Tenants Action Committee and Officers from 
various Public Sector Undertakings and Government and Financial 
Organisations, had recommended notification of guidelines dated 14.1.1992 
through a Government Resolution which has since been published in the Gazette 
of India on 8th June, 2002. A copy of the Government Resolution is annexed as 
Statement.

under the control of Public Sector Undertakings/financial institutions has 
been under consideration of the Government for some time past. 
2. To prevent arbitrary use of powers to evict genuine tenants from public 
premises and to limit the use of powers by the Estate Officers 
18 

[12 August. 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
appointed under Section 3 of the PP(E) Act, 1971, it has been decided by 
Government to lay down the following guidelines:— 
(i) The Provisions of the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised 
Occupants) Act, 1971 [P.P.(E) Act, 1971] should be used primarily 
to evict totally unauthorised occupants of the premises of public 
authorities or subletees, or employees who have ceased to be in their 
service and thus ineligible for occupation of the premises. 
(ii) The Provisions of the P.P.(E) Act, 1971 should not be resorted to 
either with a commercial motive or to secure vacant possession of 
the premises in order to accommodate their own employees, where the 
premises were in occupation of the original tenants to whom the 
premises were let either by the public authorities or the persons from 
whom the premises were acquired. 
(iii) A Person in occupation of any premises should not be treated or 
declared to be an unauthorised occupant merely on service of notice 
of termination of tenancy, but the fact of unauthorised occupation 
shall be decided by following the due procedure of law. Further, the 
contractual agreement shall not be wound up by taking advantage of 
the provisions of the P.P.(E) Act, 1971. At the same time, it will be 
open to the public authority to secure periodic revision of rent in 
terms of the provisions of the Rent Control Act in each State or to 
move under genuine grounds under the Rent Control Act for 
resuming possession. In other words, the public authorities would 
have rights similar to private Landlords under the Rent Control Act 
in dealing with genuine legal tenants. 
(iv) It is necessary to give no room for allegations that evictions were 
selectively resorted to for the pur pose of securing an unwarranted 
increase in rent, or that a change in tenancy was permitted in order to 
benefit particular individuals or institutions. In order to avoid such 
imputations or abuse of discretionary powers, the release of 
premises or change of tenancy should be decided at the level of 
Board of Directors of Public Sector Undertakings. 
19 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
(v) All the Public Undertakings should immediately review all pending 
cases before the Estate Officer or Courts with reference to these 
guidelines, and withdraw eviction proceedings against genuine 
tenants on grounds otherwise than as provided under these 
guidelines. The provisions under the P.P.(E) Act, 1971 should be 
used henceforth only in accordance with these guidelines. 
3. These orders take immediate effect.

*418. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) the sum and substance of the scientific research with regard to the 
side effects of tobacco; 
(b) whether it is a fact that 50 per cent of smokers die due to smoking and 
smoking affects their children as well; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that pan masala is one of the main causes 
for the throat cancer; 
(d) whether it is also a fact that various organisations are demanding ban on 
pan masala for the last several years; and 
24 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA

people? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (e) Scientific investigations 
have confirmed the association of smoking with various diseases and have 
provided additional evidence implicating cigarette smoking as a cause of coronary 
artery disease, stroke, obstructive lung disease, peripheral vascular disease, 
pregnancy complications including intra-uterine growth retardation and a variety 
of neoplasms including cancers of oral cavity, larynx, oesophagus, urinary 
bladder, kidney, stomach, pancreas, cervix and haematopoietic system. Recent 
studies have also established close association between Tuberculosis and 
tobacco use. As per the 40-year follow-up study conducted in the United 
Kingdom, 50 per cent of total smokers die due to smoking related diseases.

in causation of throat cancer. Various NGOs and public health agencies have 
been campaigning for a ban on pan masala.

State Governments like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra have 
already banned manufacture, storage and sale of pan masala. "The Cigarettes 
and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of 
Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Bill, 2001, introduced 
in the Rajya Sabha in March, 2001 intends to discourage the use of tobacco 
products in any form.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a ) to (d) Under the provisions of 
Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules thereunder, the responsibility for 
regulating manufacture and sale of drugs including monitoring their quality is 
vested with the State Governments. Manufacture and sale of spurious drugs is a 
clandestine activity indulged in by unlicensed and anti-social persons. Such

which belongs to another or if it is an imitation or substitute, wholly or partly of

manufacture and sale of spurious drugs. Sale of spurious drugs, if detected is 
punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years 
but which may extend to a term of life and with fine which shall not be less than 
Rs. 10,000/-. Hence there are adequate provisions in the Drugs and Cosmetics 
Act to tackle the problem of spurious drugs.

and marginalised groups of the population, in order to promote safe sex. The 
success of such intervention is determined by the environment under which the 
services are being provided. Government provides funds to State AIDS Control 
Societies for advocacy and sensitization programmes among elected representatives, 
bureaucrats, police officials etc. in order to create an enabling environment so

services under Targeted interventions projects.

Government of India has launched a comprehensive Programme, currently under 
implementation throughout the country as a centrally sponsored scheme with 
the following components:—

target populations and providing peer counselling, condom 
promotion and treatment of sexually transmitted infections. In case of 
injecting drugs users, harm reduction intervention such as needle 
exchange programme is also promoted. 
• Preventive intervention for the general population by Information, 
Education and Communication (IEC) and awareness campaign, 
provision of voluntary testing and counselling, safe blood 
transfusion services and prevention of occupational exposure. 
• Providing financial assistance for opportunistic infections, home and 
community based care. 
• Strengthening effectiveness and technical, managerial, financial 
sustainability at National, State and Municipal levels. 
• Promoting collaboration amongst public, private and voluntary 
sectors.

THE MINISTER OF STATE INTHE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) Recommendations of the report are 
mainly related to conservation, cultivation, sustainable use, quality control of 
medicinal plants and setting up of Medicinal Plants Board. 
(b) to (d) Following steps have been  taken for implementation of the 
recommendations:— 
• Medicinal Plants Board has been set up in November, 2000.

characterization of medicinal and aromatic plants.

aromatic plants have been implemented.

Guidelines for the Certification of films 
Extracts taken from Ministry of l&B's Notification No. 805/1/90-F(C) 
Dated the 6th December, 1991 Published in the Extraordinary Gazette 
of India Part II Section 3 Sub-Section (ii) 
S.0.836-(E) In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (2) of 
section 5B of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 (37 of 1952) and in supersession 
of the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Information and 
Broadcasting No. S.O. 9(E), dated the 7th January 1978, except as respects 
things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the Central 
Government hereby directs that in sanctioning films for public exhibition, the 
Board of Film Certification shall be guided by the following principles:— 
1 .The objectives of film certification will be to ensure that— 
(a)   the medium of film remains responsible and sensitive to the values 
and standards of society; 
103 

RAJYA  SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
(b) artistic expression and creative freedom are not unduly curbed; 
(c) certification is responsive to social change; 
(d) the medium of film provides clean and healthy entertainment; and 
(e) as far as possible, the film is of aesthetic value and 
cinematically of a good standard. 
2. In pursuance of the above objectives, the Board of Film Certification shall 
ensure that— 
(i) anti-social activities such as violence are not glorified or justified; 
(ii) the modus operandi of criminals, other visuals or words likely to 
incite the commission of any offence are not depicted; 
(iii) Scenes— 
(a) showing involvement of children in violence as victims or as 
perpetrators or as forced witness to violence, or showing 
children as being subjected to any form of child abuse; 
(b) Showing abuse or ridicule of physically and mentally 
handicapped persons; and 
(c) showing cruelty to, or abuse of, animals, are not presented 
needlessly; 
(iv) pointless or avoidable scenes of violence, cruelty and horror, scenes 
of violence primarily intended to provide entertainment and such 
scenes as may have the effect of desensitising or dehumanising 
people are not shown; 
(v) scenes which have the effect of justifying or glorifying drinking are 
not shown; 
(vi) Scenes tending to encourage, justify or glamorise drug addiction are 
not shown; 
(vi-a)**    Scenes tending to encourage, justify or glamorise 
consumption of tobacco or smoking are not shown; 
** Added on 15th September, 1997 
104 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA    SABHA 
(vii)  human sensibilities are not offended by vulgarity, obscenity or 
depravity; 
(viii)  such dual meaning words as obviously cater to baser 
instincts are not allowed; 
(ix)  scenes degrading or denigrating women in any manner are 
not presented; 
(x)  scenes involving sexual violence against women like 
attempt to rape, rape or any form of molestation, or scenes of 
similar nature are avoided, and if any such incident is 
germane to the theme, they shall be reduced to the 
minimum and no details are shown; 
(xi)  scenes showing sexual perversions shall be avoided and if 
such matters are germane to the theme, they shall be reduced 
to the minimum and no details are shown; 
(xii)  visuals or words contemptuous of racial, religious or other 
groups are not presented; 
(xiii)  visuals or words which promote communal, obscurantism, 
anti-scientific and anti-national attitudes are not presented; 
(xiv) the sovereignty and integrity of India is not called in 
question; 
(xv)    the security of the State is not jeopardised or endangered; 
(xvi)    friendly relations with foreign States are not strained; 
(xvii)    public order is not endangered; 
(xviii)  visuals or words involving defamation of an individual or a 
body of individuals, or contempt of court are not presented; 
EXPLANATION: Scenes that tend to create scorn, disgrace 
or disregard of rules or undermine the dignity of court will 
come under the term "contempt of Court" and 
(xix)  National symbols and emblems are not shown except in 
accordance with the provisions of the Emblems and Names 
(Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950 (12 of 1950). 
105 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
3. The Board of Film Certification shall also ensure that the film— 
(i)    is judged in its entirey from the point of view of its overall 
impact; and 
(ii)  is examined in the light of the period depicted in the film 
and the contemporary standards of the country and the 
people to which the film relates, provided that the film does 
not deprave the morality of the audience. 
4. Films that meet the above-mentioned criteria but are considered 
unsuitable for exhibition to non-adults shall be certified for exhibition to adult 
audience only. 
5. (1) While certifying films for unrestricted public exhibition, the 
Board shall ensure that the film is suitable for family viewing, that is to say, 
the film should be such that all the members of the family including children 
can view it together. 
 
(2) If the Board, having regard to the nature, content and theme of the 
film, is of the opinion that it is necessary to caution the parents/guardian to 
consider as to whether any child below the age of twelve years may be 
allowed to see such a film, the film sh all be certified for unrestricted public 
exhibition with an endorsement to that effect. 
(3) If the Board, having regard to the nature, content and theme of the 
film, is of the opinion that the exhibition of the film should be restricted to 
members of any profession or any class of persons, the film shall be certified 
for public exhibition restricted to the specialised audiences to be specified by 
the Board in this behalf. 
6. The Board shall scrutinise the titles of the films carefully and 
ensure that they are not provocative, vulgar, offensive or violative of any 
of the above-mentioned guidelines.

Following schemes are being implemented by Ministry of Social Justice and 
Empowerment and Ministry of Tribal Affairs for the welfare of Scheduled Castes, 
Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes: 
(a) Hostels 
(i) Hostels for SC boys 
(ii) Hostels for SC girls 
(iii) Hostels for ST boys 
(iv) Hostels for ST girls

Under these schemes 50% Central assistance is provided to the States and 100% 
to Union Territories for construction of Hostels. In case of Hostels for SC boys and 
girls, assistance is also provided to State Universities and NGOs (for 
expansion of existing Hostels only) on 45:45:10 matching basis. In the case of 
Central Universities, 90% Central assistance is provided. 
(b) Pre-matric Scholarships 
(a) Pre-matric Scholarship to the children of those engaged in 
unclean occupations. 
(b) Pre-matric Scholarship for OBCs. 
Under these two schemes, assistance is provided to the State Governments on 
50:50 basis (100% for Union Territory Administrations), over and above their 
respective committed liability. The scholarships vary in the range of Rs. 25 per 
month to Rs. 250 per month for 10 months apart from the ad hoc grant of Rs. 500 
per student per annum. 
(c) Post-matric Scholarships 
(a) Post Matric Scholarship for SCs. 
(b) Post Matric Scholarship for STs; and 
(c) Post Matric Scholarship for OBCs. 
For post-matric scholarships, assistance is provided on 100% basis to 
pursue education beyond matriculation inculding post-graduate courses in 
recognized institutions. The assistance includes provision for maintenance 
allowance, reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable fees, thesis 
wrting/printing charges, State tour charges etc. The maintenance allowance 
rates effective from 1.10.1995 are in between Rs.150 per month to Rs. 425 per 
month for hostellers and in between Rs. 90 per month to Rs. 190 per month 
for day scholars. The Central assistance provided to States/UTs for 
implementing the Scheme is over and above their respective committed liability, 
which they are required to bear during every year of the Plan period from their 
own resources.

Schemes for handicapped, widow, orphan children, etc. 
2762. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH SHARMAH: Will the Minister of 
SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of schemes and programmes formulated for the 
handicapped.widow, orphan children, terrorist and riot-affected children and 
women by Government; and 
(b) the basic facilities being provided to these categories by 
Government? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE 
AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRI SATYABRATA MOOKHERJEE): (a) and 
(b) The details of schemes and programmes formulated and the basic facilities 
provided thereunder for the handicapped, widows, orphaned children, terrorist 
and riot-affected children and women are annexed as Statement. 
Statement 
The details of schemes and programmes formulated and the basic 
facilities provided thereunder for the handicapped, widows, orphaned 
children, terrorist and riot-affected children and women 
1. Schemes for Disabled implemented through Ministry of Social 
Justice & Empowerment 
a. Scheme to promote Voluntary Action for Persons with 
Disabilities: It facilitates delivery of various rehabilitation 
services to persons with disabilities by public institutions 
and voluntary organizations by affording financial assistance 
and technical and administrative support under the scheme 
to promote voluntary action to enlarge the scope of vocational 
and professional opportunities, income generation and gainful 
occupations and promotes formal as well as non-formal 
employment and placement opportunities. 
b. Composite Regional Centres for Persons with Disabilities 
(CRCs) and Regional Rehabilit ation Centres (RRCs) for 
Persons with Spinal Injuries: CRCs and RRCs provide services 
for the rehabilitation of the handicapped including children. 
164 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
c. Assistance to Disabled Persons for purchase/fitting of Aids and 
Appliances (ADIP): The objective of the Scheme is to assist the 
needy disabled persons in procuring durable, sophisticated and 
scientifically manufactured, standard aids and appliances that can 
promote their physical, social and psychological rehabilitation 
by reducing the effects of disabilities and enhancing their 
economic potential. 
2. Schemes for widows implemented through Department of 
Women and Child Development (Ministry of Human Resource 
Development) and Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 
a. Swadhar: Widows deserted by their families and relatives 
are benefited under this scheme. 
b. General Grant in Aid Programme for financial assistance: 
Under this scheme also widows are rehabilitated. 
3. Schemes for orphaned children implemented through 
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 
Scheme of Assistance to Homes (Shishu Greh) for children to 
promote in-Country Adoption: Under the scheme, adoption of 
children is promoted. 
4. Schemes for terrorist and riot-affected children and women 
implemented through Ministry of Home Affairs 
Reimbursement of Security Related Expenditure: An amount of Rs. 
1.00 lakh is reimbursed to concerned North Eastern State 
Governments where a civilian is killed in militancy related 
violence and payment is made-to the next of kin of the victim by 
the concerned State Government.

TRIFED Procurement Centres 
2769. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the number ofTRIFED procurement centres in the country as on date 
alongwith the details for last three years, State-wise; 
(b) the percentage of tribal population getting benefited from the service 
ofTRIFED during the last three years, State-wise; 
(c) whether it is a facts that tribals often sell their produce either to the 
middlemen or in the open market because of the improper services of TRIFED 
and physical inaccessibility; and 
(d) if so, the steps Government propose to take for improving the 
services and setting up more procurement centres? 
THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JUAL ORAM): (a) 
TRIFED, have 104 procurement centres operating directly through marketing 
cooperative societies. The details are given at Statement-I. (See below). 
Besides direct procurement,TRIFED also undertakes such operations through the 
STDCCs, State Forest Development Corporations, Vandhan Samities and Large 
Area Multi-Purpose Societies (LAMPS) of different States.The details of the 
centres operated by such agencies are given at Statement-I I. (See below) 
(b)The activities ofTRIFED are restricted to the predominantly tribal 
areas. It is not possible to quantify the percentage. 
(c) and (d) Although it is a fact that tribals sometimes sell their produce 
to the middlemen or in the open market, but it is not because of improper 
service of TRIFED or its physical inaccessibility. In a bid to meet their urgent 
economic needs, the tribals sometimes sell their produce to local traders as an 
advance sale against the money borrowed by them which is generally before the 
harvest of the crop. As already mentioned earlier, TRIFED with a large 
network of procurement centre, operating

been procuring large quantities of MFPs/SAPS from the tribal areas. However,

produce and also on the exigencies as envisaged by TRIFED.

2770. SHRIURKHAO GWRA BRAHMA: Will the Minister ofTRIBAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the budgetary allocation for tribal development in the country 
during trie current financial year, State-wise; 
(b) whether it is a fact that huge amount of money had been diverted by the 
State Governments to other sectors from the budget allocated for the Tribal 
Affairs; and . 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the appropriate action taken by 
Government to stop unscrupulous diversion of funds? 
THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFA IRS (SHRI JUAL ORAM): (a) 
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs allo cates Funds State-wise for tribal 
development in the country under two schemes viz. Grants under Article 
275(1) of the Constitution of India and Special Central Assistance to the 
Tribal Sub- Plan (SC A to TSP). A statement showing the State-wise 
budgetary allocation made to different States under Article 275(1) of the 
Constitution of India during the current financial year is attached (See 
below).The allocation under SCA toTSP has not been finalized pending 
approval of the revised guidelines by the Planning Commission. 
(b) and (c) In the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of 
India for the year ended March. 1998. it has, inter-alia been brought out that 
scrutiny of records in selected districts of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, 
Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, 
Rajasthan, Sikkim,Tamil Nadu.Tnpura. West Bengal and Daman and Diu 
revealed that funds aggregating Rs. 85.88 crores, which pertain to Special 
Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Plan were diverted to other schemes/ 
activities.These observations are based on a sample check of documents for 
the period 1992—98 of the Ministry and the implementing departments and 
agencies of 17 States and one U.T.The matter has since been taken up with 
the State Governments concerned. 
The following efforts are made to ensure proper utilistion of funds by 
the States/UTs.: 
1. Utilisation Certificates are insisted upon as a pre-requisite for the 
further release of funds; 
2. Periodic progress reports regarding the status of implementation of 
schemes are obtained and reviewed; 
3. Central Government Officers visit the States/UTs to ascertain the 
progress of implementation of schemes/projects; 
4. Meetings/conferences are convened with the Secretaries of the 
States'Tribal Welfare Departments and other officials to ensure 
timely submission of proposals for the released of funds and to 
speed i 'p the implementation of schemes;

Implementation Committees of the ITDPs at the Block levels and 
the Panchayat Samitis Monitor timely spending of funds and 
effective implementation of schemes.

Workshop on Transport Policy in the Capital 
2783. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the issues which were debated in the Workshop on Transport 
Policy held in the Capital from 4th June, 2002, as reported in theTimes of 
India, dated the 1st June, 2002; 
 
(b) the salient recommendations made by the group to control 
pollution, ease congestion, control accidents and provide safe and 
comfortable transport system in metropolitan cities: and 
(c) the action taken by Government on these recommendations 
specially to provide relief to the citizens of the Capital? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): 
(a) The following issues were debated in the four technical sessions 
conducted in the workshop:— 
(i)    Issues in Urban Transport Policy; 
(ii)    Resource Generation (Financing) for Urban Transport; 
(iii)    Issues in Mass (Public) Transport and Urban Road Transport; 
(iv)    Institutional Issues in Urban Transport. 
(b)The recommendations made in the Workshop include:— 
- giving explicit priority to mass transport over personalized 
transport; 
- implementation ofTransport Systems management measures; 
- the integration of land use and transport planning; 
- setting up a designated agency for planning and coordination of 
Urban Transport issues; 
- setting up of Special Purpose Vehicles for funding larger Urban 
Transport projects and tapping other sources such as'user charges, 
share of fuel taxes, parking revenue etc. for generating resources; 
- preparation of a comprehensive legislation for UrbanTransport.

initiate consultations with the State Governments as transport is a State

*317. DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: Will the Minister of INFORMATION 
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state:

THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING 
(SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ): (a) to (d) The Cable Television Networks 
(Regulation) Act, 1995 was passed with a view to regulating the operation of 
cable television networks in the country. Ever since, the Government has 
been monitoring the implementation of this Act and its benefit to the end 
users. On the basis of feedback received, some amendments were made in 
this Act vide the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Amendment Act 
2000 to inter-alia define the "authorised officers", make the Programme and 
Advertising Codes applicable to all channels/programmes when transmitted 
or retransmitted through a cable service and empower the "authorised 
officers" to take action for violations of Programme and Advertising Codes.

Advertising Code, the Government has also constituted two committees

Ministries of Information and Broa dcasting, Home Affairs, External 
Affairs, Defence and Law to render advice on the violations of the 
Programme Code; and 
(ii) A Committee consisting of officers from the Ministries of 
Information and Broadcasting, Women and Child Development, Health 
and Law and representative from the Advertising Standards Council of 
India to look into the violations of Advertising Code including cases 
of surrogate advertising.

Under-Valuation of Maruti Udyog Ltd. 
†*319. SHRI D.P.YADAV: Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for which the Maruti Udyog Limited has been sold to 
Suzuki Motor Corporation; 
(b) whether the actual assets of Maruti Udyog were underassessed and it 
was sold at a throw-away price; and 
(c) whether a guarantee has been taken from the Suzuki Motor 
Corporation to the effect that their Management will not retrench the 
employees by showing losses? 
THE MINISTER OF DISINVESTMENT (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) 
Government established Maruti Udyog Ltd. (MUL) as a Government company 
in 1981 with the objectives of modernizing Indian automobile industry; 
production of fuel-efficient vehicle to conserve scarce resources and production of 
large number of vehicles necessary for economic growth. Later Government 
entered into an agreement with Suzuki Motor 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
232 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
Corporation (SMC) in 1982 with an equity sharing of 74% and 26% between 
Government and SMC respectively as SMC brought the technology. By 
1987, Government allowed the shareholding of SMC to go up to 40%. 
Subsequently in 1992, Government further allowed the shareholding of SMC 
to increase to 50% with the Government shareholding reducing to 49.74%, each 
stage resulting in gradual transfer of increased management control to SMC. 
Initially, MUL remained the undisputed market leader with a market share 
peaking to 83% and profits rising highest to Rs.652 crore during 1997-98. 
Onset of liberalization and the entry of many international car majors in the 
Indian market, however, resulted in increased competition and the profits and 
market share of MUL went down. Government noted that the objectives of 
setting up MUL had been realized and there is no strategic purpose it can fulfil 
by holding on to MUL shares as further holding of these shares would lead to 
an erosion in value. Government realised that in a consumer driven market 
like the automobiles sector, the Government needs to become a neutral 
arbitrator/regulator for the entire industry rather than co-owner of one of the 
companies. Further, the Government would not be in a position to invest 
further in the equity capital of MUL that was required for introducing new 
models, upgradation of production facilites, etc. Hence, Government has decided 
to exit from MUL as quickly as possible. The decision to exit from MUL by 
the Government was also in line with the overall policy of the Government to 
exit from all non-strategic areas, which includes auto sector as well. 
In line with the steps adopted earlier and the above policy, the 
Government decided a two stage disinvestment of its holding in MUL. In the 
first phase, a rights issue of Rs.400 crore has been completed with SMC 
subscribing to the total rights issue, including rights shares renounced by 
Government in favour of SMC. SMC also paid Rs.1000 crore control premium 
to Government. This contrasts with the 'nil' amount that Government took 
while transferring control progressively in earlier stages. The Revised Joint 
Venture Agreement (RJVA) entered into between SMC and Government 
envisages that, in the second phase, the existing shares of Government 
(approximately 65.80 lakh) would be sold through a public offer.

Fourteenth International HIV-AIDS Conference 
1945. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: 
SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: 
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a high power delegation of Government 
attended the 14th International HIV-AIDS Conference held in Spain recently; 
(b) if so, the details of members .of the delegation; and 
(c) what was the country's proposal to fight AIDS in the Conference and to 
what extent the country benefited from the deliberations of the Conference? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. A high power 
delegation was led by the Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare, Shri 
Shatrughan Sinha. Other members of the delegation were Director General 
Health Services, Dr. S.P. Agarwal; Additional Secretary and Project Director, 
National AIDS Control Organization, Smt. Meenakshi Datta Ghosh and Joint 
Secretary from the Office of Prime Minister Shri Chattar Singh. 
(c) Government of India highlighted the various aspects of the National 
AIDS Control Programme touching upon the following issues: 
(a) Reducing the spread of HIV in groups at high risk by 
identification of target populations and providing peer 
counselling, condom promotion, treatment of sexually 
transmitted infections etc.; 
(b) Preventive intervention for the general population by 
Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and awareness 
campaigns, provision of voluntary testing and counselling, safe 
blood transfusion services and prevention of occupational exposure; 
(c) Upscaling of Prevention of Mother to Child Transmission 
Programme; 
275 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
(d) Care and support to people living with HIV/AIDS including 
treatment of opportunistic infections; and 
(e) Inter-sectoral collaboration among public, private & NGO 
sectors. 
Based on discussions with experts at conference, the following lessons 
were learnt: 
(i) India needs a much higher commitment of resources to upscale and 
extend outreach and coverage of its targeted interventions for 
prevention and care to persons infected with HIV/AIDS; 
(ii) India needs to articulate clearly its stand on what will constitute care 
and support for persons affected with HIV/AIDS; 
(iii) India needs to examine the availability and costing of generic drugs 
indigenously produced, and may initiate a dialogue with the 
pharmaceutical industry; and 
(iv) Effective efforts for prevention need to be put in place, that will 
combine education, information and delivery of services to bring 
about behavioural change.

HIV-Free Certificates for foreigners 
1960. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of 
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether with a view to checking the spread of HIV virus 
Government propose to insist on HIV-free certificates from foreigners 
visiting India; 
whether the Ministry of Tourism and the Ministry of External Affairs have 
been consulted in this regard; 
if so, what is their reaction; and 
by when a final decision is expected to be taken? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) As per policy of the Government, all 
foreigners, intending to stay for more than one year in India and those 
294 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
foreigners who enter India on short term visa but want to extend their stay for a 
year or more, must undergo testing for HIV and AIDS once during their stay. 
However, foreigners working in various missions whether enjoying 
diplomatic status or not; foreign priests and nuns and foreign journalists 
accredited to the PIB (Press Information Bureau of India) are excluded from 
the testing fof HIV and AIDS. 
(b) to (d) In order to examine the issue, a meeting of experts was held on 
15-6-99 which was attended to by the representatives fromW.H.O., Indian Council 
for Cultural Relations (ICC.R), National Institute of Communicable Diseases 
(N.I.CD), Ministry of Home Affairs,-A.I.I.M.S. New Delhi, Lady Harding 
Medical College (LHMC), New Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, New 
Delhi, Ministry of External Affairs, U.N. AIDS, National AIDS Research 
Institute, Pune and National Law School of India, Bangalore.The Ministry of 
Tourism did not participate in the meeting.The experts were of the opinion that 
mandatory HIV testing on foreigners/ foreign students is contrary to the 
recommendations of the World Health Organisation. 
The issue was again discussed in the 15th meeting of the National 
AIDS Control Board held on 3rd August, 1999 under the Chairmanship of 
Health Secretary and the Board agreed with the opinion of the experts and 
gave its concurrence for revising the policy on HIV testing for foreigners 
including foreign students. The revised policy has since been approved by the 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

Immunization Programme for children 
1963. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 51 per cent of the child population are not fully 
immunized and 74 percent suffer from anaemia; 
(b) if so, what steps Government have taken to address this problem; 
(c) whether State Governments have any special plan in this regard; and 
(d) if so, the details of the same for the last three years? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to ;d) As user UNICEF evaluation, the 
percentage of fully-immunized children in the s. ,untry against the six vaccine-
preventable diseases namely childhood tuberculosis, diptheria, pertussis, 
poliomyelitis, measles and neo-natal tetanus in 2000-2001 was 53.6%. As per the 
National Family Health Survey-2 (1998-99), 74.3 per cent of the children (6-34 
months) suffer from anaemia in varying degrees. 
Under the Universal Immunization Programme, being implemented by the 
Government of India through the States, vaccination is available to the children 
throughout the country for control of six vaccine-preventable diseases. Under 
the Reproductive and Child Health Programme, implemented by the Government 
of India through the States, anaemic children in the age group 1-5 years are given 
100 tablets of Iron and Folic Acid (small). These drugs are supplied to the 
sub-centres as a part of the Drug Kit A. 
As a part of the Immunization Strengthening Project, the RCH 
Outreach Scheme is being implemented to improve the delivery of 
immunization and other maternal and child health services in remote and 
comparatively weak 151 districts of various States.

Japanese Encephalitis in Andhra Pradesh 
1988. DR. DASARI NARAYANA RAO: Will the Minister of HEALTH 
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) the status of Japanese Encephalitis this year in the State of Andhra 
Pradesh which is quite prone to this dreaded disease; 
(b) whether endemic districts of this disease have been identified in the 
State; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the measures taken by Government in these districts in particular and the 
State as a whole? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) No incidence of Japanese 
Encephalitis (JE) has been reported from the State of Andhra Pradesh, during 
the current year (upto June, 2002). 
(b) and (c) Out of total 23 districts, 16 districts in the State have 
reported occurrence of JE. There has been a decline in reported cases and 
deaths during 2001 as compared to previous two years. 
(d)The preventive and control measures taken are as under:— 
 Vaccination of high risk population group. 
 Vector control by indoor residual spray and anti-larval operations and 
fogging with Malathion.

Statement-I 
The salient features and advertisements code followed by All India Radio 
and Doordarshan and prescribed under Cable Television Networks (Regulation) 
Act, 1995 are as follows:— 
1. Advertising shall be so designed as to conform to the laws of the 
country and should not offend morality, decency and religious 
susceptibilities of the people. 
2. No advertisement shall be permitted which— 
(i)    Derides any race, caste, colour, creed and nationality; 
337 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
(ii) is against any of the directive principles, or any other 
provision of the Constitution of India; 
(iii) tends to incite people to crime, cause disorder or violence, or 
breach of law of glorifies violence or obscenity in any way; 
(iv)  presents criminality as desirable. 
(v)   adversely affects friendly relations with foreign States; 
(vi) exploits the national emblem, or any part of the Constitution or the 
person or personality of a national leader or State Dignitary; 
(vii) relates to or promotes cigarettes and tobacco products, liquor, 
wines and other intoxicants; 
(viii) in its depiction of women violates the constitutional 
guarantees to all citizens such as equality of status and 
opportunity and dignity of the individual. In particular, no 
advertisement shall be permitted which projects a derogatory 
image of women. Women must not be portrayed in a manner that 
emphasises passive, submissive qualities and encourages them 
to play a subordinate, secondary role in the family and 
society, the portrayal of men and women should not encourage 
mutual disrespect. Advertiser shall ensure that the portrayal of the 
female form is tasteful and aesthetic, and is within the well-
established norms of good taste and decency. 
3. No advertisement message shall in any way be presented as News. 
4. No advertisement shall be permitted the objects whereof are wholly 
or mainly of a religious or political nature; advertisements must not be 
directed towards any religious or political end or have any relation 
to any industrial dispute. 
5. The goods advertised shall not suffer from any defect or deficiency 
as mentioned in Consumer Protection Act, 1986. 
6. No advertisement, which endangers the safety of children or 
338 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
creates in them any interest in unhealthy practices or shows them 
begging or in an undignified or Indecent manner shall be accepted. 
7. No advertisement shall contain references which are likely to lead 
the public to infer that the product advertised or any of its ingredients 
has some special or miraculous or super-natural property or quality, 
which is difficult or being proved, e.g. cure for baldness, skin 
whitener, etc. 
8. The picture and the audible matter of the advertisement shall not be 
excessively 'loud'. 
9. No advertisement shall be accepted which violates AIR andTV 
Broadcast Code, which is reproduced below: 
(i)      criticism of friendly countries; 
(ii)     attack on religions or communities; 
(iii)     anything obscence or defamatory; 
(iv)    incitement to violence or anything against maintenance of law 
and order; 
(v)     anything amounting to contempt of court; 
(vi)     aspersions against the integrity of the President and Judiciary; 
(vii)   anything affecting the integrity of the Nation; and 
(viii)   criticism by name of any person. 
10. Indecent, vulgar, suggestive, repulsive or-offensive themes or 
treatment shall be avoided in all advertisements. 
Statement-ll 
Salient features of norms of journalistic conduct 
Advertisements: 
(1) Commercial advertisements are information as much as social, 
economic or political information. When more, advertisements' 
339 

RAJYA SABHA [12 August, 2002] 
shape attitude and ways of life at least as much, as other kinds of 
information, comment, journalistic propriety demands that 
avertisements must be clearly distinguishable from edited matters 
carried in the newspaper. 
(2) Newspaper shall not publish anything which has a tendency to 
malign wholesale or hurt the religious sentiments of any 
community or section of society. 
(3) Advertisements which offend the provisions of the Drugs and 
Magical Remedies (Objectionable Advertisement) Act, 1954, 
should be rejected. 
(4) Newspapers should not publish an advertisement containing 
anything which is unlawful or illegal, or contrary to good taste or to 
journalistic ethics or proprieties. 
(5) Newspapers while publishing advertisements, shall specify the 
amount received by them. The rationable behind this is that 
advertisements should be charged at rates usually chargeable by a 
newspaper since payment or more than the normal rates would 
amount to a subsidy to the paper. 
(6) Publication of dummy advertisements that neither been paid for, 
nor authorized by the advertiser to constitute breach of journalistic 
ethics. 
(7) Deliberate failure to publish an advertisement in all the copies of a 
newspaper offends against the standard of journalistic ethics and 
constitutes gross professional misconduct. 
(8) Newspapers/journalist shall not publish anything which is obscene, 
vulgar or offensive to public good taste. 
(9) Newspapers shall not display advertisements which are vulgar or 
which through depiction of a woman in nude or lewd posture, provoke 
lecherous attention of males as if she herself was a commercial 
commodity for sale.

KRISHNAMURTHY): (a) Yes, Sir.

The Supreme Court v/'ctetheir judgement dated 1.6.1996 in the case of 
Common Cause Vs. Union of India and others passed certain directions regarding 
trial of criminal cases on priority basis, and directed all the High Courts to 
issue necessary directions in that behalf to all the criminal courts under their 
control and supervision. The directions are intended to release undertrials 
languishing in jails for long periods even beyond the prescribed period of the 
punishment, specially in petty offences. 
The Supreme Court in Its orders dated 13.10.99 and 6.12.99 in R.D. 
Upadhyaya's case expressed concern over the plight of undertrials who are in 
jails. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has also stressed the need for taking 
effective steps for filing challans/reports particularly in cases which

involve petty offences and in which the undertrials have been in jails for a long 
time. Based on the above direction of the Supreme Courts, the Central Government 
vide their letter dated 17.12.1999 requested all the State Governments/UT 
Administration to take urgent necessary steps to mitigate the hardships face by the 
undertrials.

recognition of the centrality of the Gram Sabha in the Panchayati Raj System.

various States/UTs including Schedule-V areas.

Setting up of Food Banks 
2042. SHRIYADLAPATIVENKAT RAO: Will the Minister of TRIBAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether with a view to making the country hunger-free, Government 
propose to set-up Food Bank for the poor people; 
(b) whether a target date for making India hunger-free by 15th August, 2007 
has been fixed; and 
(c) if so, the details in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JUAL ORAM): (a) to 
(c) A Central Sector Scheme for the setting up of Village Grain Banks in tribal 
villages was launched in 1996-97. It is a continuing scheme, under which there 
is no target date for making India hunger-free. 
The Village Grain Bank Scheme was launched in selected areas 
identified by the Central Planning Committee (CPC) as a preventive measure 
against the death of tribal people due to starvation. The scheme provides that 
villagers in identified areas can form a committee and set up Grain Banks. This 
Ministry provides a one-time grant for setting up Grain Banks with an 
allocation of 100 kg. of locally consumed food grains per family. The members 
borrow from this bank in time of need and repay after the harvest or on getting 
income as wages. Under the scheme, funds are released to the State 
Governments through TRIFED.The CPC has identified 370 blocks in 52 
districts in 13 States for implementation of the scheme. However, the list is 
indicative and the State Governments can select villages/blocks outside these 
areas, if considered necessary. Under the scheme, an amount of Rs. 1024.37 
lakh has so far been released to the States for establishment of 1876 Grain 
Banks.

The Centrally sponsored scheme of Low Cost Sanitation Scheme for 
Libration of Scavengers (LCS) is being implemented by this Ministry since

from the obnoxious practice of carrying head loads of night soil and the 
scheme is being implemented on a whole town basis. 
The scheme is being operated by providing subsidy from this Ministry and 
loans from Housing and Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO) in a 
synchronized manner so that the conversion/construction of low cost 
sanitation units and liberation of scavengers is done on a whole town basis.

Separate authority for conservation of water bodies 
2045. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any separate authority has been constituted for 
conservation and management of all water bodies; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) if not, how the need to conserve lakhs of ponds etc. would be taken 
care of? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): 
(a) to (c) A National River Conservation Authority exists under the 
Chairmanship of Prime Minister to finalise the policy framework and oversee the 
implementation of conservation and manaqement plans of rivers and lakes. A 
Water Quality Assessment Authority has been constituted under the provisions 
of Environment (Protection) Act,1986 in May, 2001 with Secretary of the 
Ministry of Environment & Forests as Chairman for water quality management of 
surface and ground water bodies. A National River Conservation Plan is under 
implementation for conservation and pollution 
400 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
abatement of polluted rivers. Under this Plan, conservation and pollution 
abatement works have been approved in 153 towns along the polluted 
stretches of 28 rivers in 17 States. The estimated cost of these works is Rs.3343 
crore against which Central grants amounting to Rs.1068 crore have been 
released so far. Conservation and management of rivers is one of the monitorable 
targets under the Tenth Plan. For conservation and management of lakes, a 
National Lake Conservation Plan is under implementation. Under this 
scheme, plans for conservation and management of 7 urban polluted lakes, 
have been approved at an estimated cost  of Rs.27.22 crore.These projects are 
under implementation and Central grants amounting to Rs.9.79 crore have been 
released to the State Governments concerned so far.

In June, 1997 it was decided to carry out amendments to the Delhi Rent Act, 
1995 before bringing it into force. Accordingly, the Delhi Rent (Amendment) 
Bill, 1997 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 28.7.1997. The Bill was referred 
to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Urban & Rural Development to 
examine and report. The Committee examined the Bill in detail and submitted 
its report on 21.12.2000 suggesting a few more changes.The Government 
considered the Report of the Committee and accepted all its recommendations.

given to the Secretary-General, Rajya Sabha. At present the Bill is pending 
before the Rajya Sabha for its consideration. After the Bill is passed by the 
Parliament and assented to by the President, the Delhi Rent Act, 1995 along 
with amendments will be brought into force.

New guidelines for access to Urban Infrastructure Fund 
2050. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether based on Census 2001 figures, Government are planning to 
revamp the urban development strategy by framing fresh guidelines for those 
States that want to access the Urban Infrastructure Fund; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the rv»wly proposed Urban Incentive Fund Scheme will apply 
only to fast growing small cities with a population between 1—5 million; and 
(d) if so, the names of cities identified for Urban Incentive Fund 
Scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (SHRI O. 
RAJAGOPAL): (a) and (b) In his Budget Speech for 2002-2003, the Finance 
Minister has announced creation of an Urban Reforms Incentive Fund with an 
outlay of Rs. 500 crores. State-wise allocation of this amount have been 
tentatively decided by the Planning Commission on the basis of percentage of 
urban population of each State/UT. However, actual release will be made after 
ascertaining action taken by the State Government towards urban reforms. 
In the initial phase, the reforms linked Central assistance would be given 
for the following: 
1. Repeal of the Urban Land Ceiling and Regulation Act at the State 
level by Resolution; 
2. Rationalization of Stamp Duty in phases to bring it down to no more 
than 5% by the end of the Tenth Plan period; 
3. Reform of Rent Control Laws to remove rent control so as to 
stimulate private investment in rental housing; 
4. Introduction of computerised processes of registration; 
5. Reform of Property Tax so that it may become a major source of 
revenue of urban local bodies, and arrangements for its 
404 
 

[12 August, 2002] RAJYA   SABHA 
effective implementation so that collection efficiency reaches at 
least 85% by the end of Tenth Plan period; 
6. Levy of reasonable user charges by Urban Local Bodies, with the 
objective that full cost of O & M (Operation & Maintenance) is 
collected by end of the Tenth Plan period; 
7. Introduction of double entry system of accounting in Urban Local 
Bodies. 
(c) and (d)The proposed Central assistance under Urban Reforms 
Incentive Fund will be provided only to those States which agree to carry out the 
reforms agenda as per Memorandum of Agreement to be signed between the 
Central and State Government.This will not be linked to any particular city.

2052.   SHRI N.R. DASARI: 
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the steps taken for increasing the powers and improving the 
financial position of the local bodies after the 73rd and 74th Constitution 
Amendments were passed;

financial position of the local bodies; and

DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (,SHRI O.

with the Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992 relating to Panchayati 
Raj, have informed that State Governments and U.T. Administration are being 
pursued to develop more powers to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), both

State-level Pooled Financing Structure, Tax-free Municipal Bonds, Property 
Tax Reforms, etc. In pursuance of the 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts, the
